purpose: Test the natural inductive strategy suggested by the structural theorem that every essentially 6-edge-connected 4-regular graph is obtained from K5 by 2-extensions. Prove the exact colouring condition for an inverse 2-reduction and exhibit a colourable essentially-6 Hamiltonian graph for which every admissible 2-reduction parent is non-3-colourable. Thus 3-colourability cannot be propagated by plain parent-graph recursion along the structural construction tree.

source_structure.two_extension: Choose two independent edges ab and cd, delete them, add a new vertex v, and add va,vb,vc,vd.
source_structure.two_reduction: Conversely, at a degree-four vertex v choose a perfect matching {{a,b},{c,d}} of N(v), delete v, and add ab and cd when this yields a simple graph in the required structural class.
source_structure.structural_theorem: Every essentially 6-edge-connected 4-regular graph is obtainable from K5 by a sequence of 2-extensions; equivalently every non-K5 member has a structural 2-reduction sequence back to K5.

colour_preservation_lemma.name: TWO_REDUCTION_PRESERVES_A_FIXED_THREE_COLOURING_IFF_THE_NEIGHBOUR_SPLIT_IS_2_PLUS_2_AND_THE_PAIRING_CROSSES
colour_preservation_lemma.statement: Let phi be a proper 3-colouring of a 4-regular graph G and v a vertex. Since all neighbours of v avoid phi(v), N(v) uses at most the other two colours. A perfect-matching 2-reduction at v preserves phi restricted to G-v exactly when both added matching edges join different colours. Such a perfect matching exists iff the four neighbour colours split 2+2. In that case exactly two of the three perfect matchings cross the two colour classes. For a 3+1 or 4+0 split every perfect matching contains a monochromatic pair.
proof: The only new constraints in the parent graph are the two added matching edges, so the restricted colouring is proper iff each matched pair receives different colours.
With only two available neighbour colours, two disjoint bichromatic pairs use exactly two vertices of each colour, giving the necessary 2+2 condition.

Conversely a 2+2 split has exactly two perfect matchings consisting entirely of cross-colour pairs; the third matches equal colours. A 3+1 or 4+0 multiset leaves a same-colour pair in every perfect matching.

finite_control.essential_6_control: The checker exhausts every nontrivial vertex shore 2<=|S|<=5 and finds minimum cut size six; hence there is no nontrivial edge cut of size below six.
finite_control.neighbour_pattern: For every one of the 24 proper 3-colourings and every one of the 10 vertices, the four neighbour colours have multiplicities 3+1. No vertex in any solution has a 2+2 neighbour split.

all_admissible_reductions.definition: Enumerate every vertex and all three perfect matchings of its four neighbours. Keep exactly the pairings whose two added edges are nonedges of G-v and whose parent is simple, connected, 4-regular and essentially 6-edge-connected.
all_admissible_reductions.exact_result: Every one of the 12 admissible parent graphs has zero proper 3-colourings. The checker verifies this by exhaustive 3^9 evaluation for every parent.

main_theorem.name: COLOURABLE_ESSENTIALLY6_GRAPH_WITH_NO_COLOURABLE_ADMISSIBLE_2REDUCTION_PARENT
main_theorem.statement: There exists a simple essentially 6-edge-connected 4-regular Hamiltonian graph G such that G is 3-colourable but every admissible 2-reduction parent of G is not 3-colourable.
proof: The finite control checker verifies all graph-structural properties and finds 24 proper 3-colourings of G.
It exhausts all vertex/pairing choices and finds exactly 12 admissible 2-reduction parents.
Each of those 12 parents has zero proper 3-colourings by exhaustive exact evaluation.
Independently, every solution of G has a 3+1 neighbour split at every vertex, so the local colour-preservation lemma already forbids restricting any solution through any 2-reduction.

killed: The recurrence 3COL(G) iff there exists an admissible structural 2-reduction parent H with 3COL(H).
An induction that follows the K5-to-G 2-extension characterization while storing only the parent graph and one parent 3-colouring.
The hope that every colourable essentially-6 4-regular graph has some colour-compatible 2-reducible vertex.
positive: The exact obstruction to colour-preserving reduction is localized: inverse elimination of v must retain the four-neighbour NAD4 relation rather than replace it only by two graph edges.
The structural 2-extension theorem can still serve as a decomposition skeleton if the algorithm carries a richer boundary/CSP state through reductions.
not_killed: A polynomial symbolic recurrence carrying NEQ plus NAD4 or another compact boundary relation instead of plain parent graphs.
A different reduction sequence with non-graph constraints accumulated and later eliminated globally.

next_target.name: E8_2REDUCTION_NEQ_NAD4_SYMBOLIC_STATE_V7_1
next_target.directive: Stop plain graph-only induction on 2-reductions. Derive the exact constraint language produced by repeatedly eliminating degree-four vertices: original graph edges give NEQ_3 and each eliminated vertex gives NAD4 on its four neighbours. Test whether the resulting three-state CSP admits a polynomial closure/elimination or whether its projected relations generate a known hard clone. Any candidate must handle the v7.0 control without branching over the 24 colourings or over three pairings per reduction.

sources: EGRES Technical Report 2022-13 / Jordan--Huang--Simmons--Weatherspoon--Zheng: every essentially 6-edge-connected 4-regular graph is obtainable from K5 by 2-extensions.
